title: Fine-tuning a 350M Model for Better Structured Outputs in 100 GRPO Steps
gist: A fully public GRPO recipe (TRL, ~500 samples, 100 steps, free-tier GPU) lifts LiquidAI's 350M-parameter LFM2.5 model's IFStruct structured-output score from 22.6% to 29.7%, closing but not eliminating the gap to a much larger Qwen3.5-2B model (33.15%).

insights.claim: Structured-output compliance (whether a model reliably returns valid, parseable output in the requested schema) is usually folded into broader reasoning/extraction benchmarks rather than measured on its own, even though it often determines whether a model can be wired into a downstream production system at all.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: Investors evaluating small/cheap LLMs for production pipelines should demand a standalone schema-compliance score, not just aggregate reasoning benchmarks, since compliance is what gates deployability.
insights.quote: Whether a model reliably returns valid, parseable output in the requested format and shape — schema compliance — is often what decides whether it can be wired into a downstream system at all.

insights.claim: The base LiquidAI LFM2.5-350M model scored 22.6% on the IFStruct structured-output benchmark (2000 samples) when served locally via llama.cpp, close to the 21.1% reported in the original IFStruct release blog.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: Establishes a reproducible baseline; small variance between independent evaluation setups (21.1% vs 22.6%) is a useful sanity bound when comparing benchmark claims across labs.

insights.claim: After a GRPO fine-tuning run of ~500 samples and 100 steps, the same model's overall IFStruct score rose from 22.6% to 29.7% (+7.1 points), with JSON-format pass rate nearly doubling (18.0% to 31.9%, +13.9) while YAML pass rate barely changed (27.2% to 27.5%, +0.3).
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: A cheap, few-hundred-sample RL fine-tune can materially move production-relevant compliance metrics; the gains track precisely the dimensions targeted by data augmentation, evidence the method is genuinely mechanistic rather than lucky.

insights.claim: Bare-list (top-level array) output compliance jumped from 16.6% to 29.7% (+13.1 points) after training, while wrapper-key compliance moved only slightly (28.5% to 29.7%, +1.2), matching the fact that only the bare-list/array format was specifically targeted by prompt augmentation during training.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: Confirms the improvement is attributable to the specific training-data augmentation choices (fenced-code and array-wrapping prompts), not generic RL fine-tuning magic — a reusable pattern for closing specific benchmark gaps cheaply.

insights.claim: Despite the gains, the GRPO-tuned 350M model's 29.7% IFStruct score still trails the reported 33.15% score of the much larger Qwen3.5-2B model.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: Tempers the headline improvement: cheap task-specific fine-tuning narrows but does not close the capability gap to a model roughly 6x larger, so parameter count still buys real advantage on this task.

insights.claim: Even after GRPO fine-tuning, the single most common failure mode by far remained 'required field missing' (7,331 occurrences post-training vs 7,228 pre-training), meaning the dominant error type did not meaningfully improve despite the higher headline pass rate.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: Headline benchmark deltas can mask persistent, unresolved failure modes; investors should read error-type breakdowns, not just top-line pass rates, when assessing whether a fine-tune actually fixed the underlying reliability problem.

insights.claim: Per-task results are highly uneven even after training: entity types like camera_review and gpu_review stayed near 6-7% pass rate post-training, while others like event_ticket_booking reached 57.9% — the model's structured-output reliability varies enormously by task domain.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: A single aggregate benchmark score can obscure domains where a small fine-tuned model remains unreliable; teams should check task-level breakdowns before deploying into a specific schema-heavy use case.

themes.theme: Recipe: cheap compute, targeted data, layered reward

insights.claim: The entire GRPO fine-tuning run (~500 training samples, 100 steps) is sized to run on a free-tier Colab or Kaggle GPU, making this a near-zero-cost recipe for improving a small open model's schema compliance.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: Signals that meaningful compliance gains for small open-weight models are achievable at near-zero marginal training cost, lowering the bar for teams to self-improve small models rather than pay for larger hosted ones.

insights.claim: Because LFM2.5-350M uses a hybrid attention/convolution architecture, the LoRA adapter had to target LFM-specific module names (q_proj/k_proj/v_proj/out_proj/in_proj plus w1/w2/w3), training only about 6M parameters, roughly 1.66% of the full model.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: A concrete, reusable gotcha: non-standard/hybrid model architectures require architecture-specific LoRA target-module lists, or fine-tuning silently under-trains the model.

insights.claim: The reward function combines three components on a weighted sum (json_format_reward, field_count_reward, schema_validation_reward with weights 1.0/0.5/2.0), where schema validation counts every constraint violation and gates partial credit on required-key coverage.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: Illustrates a reusable multi-term reward-shaping pattern for compliance-focused RL fine-tuning that other teams can copy for their own schema/format tasks.

insights.claim: Training data augmentation deliberately closed two known gaps between the Nemotron training distribution and the IFStruct eval distribution: 40% of prompts got an appended 'fenced code block' instruction, and a disjoint 20% were converted into top-level-array tasks requiring bare-list output with a specific item count.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: Shows that matching the training data's format distribution to the eval/production distribution is often more impactful than the RL algorithm itself — a transferable lesson for anyone fine-tuning against a specific downstream benchmark.

insights.claim: The full recipe (notebook, dataset nvidia/Nemotron-RL-instruction_following-structured_outputs, IFStruct benchmark repo Liquid4All/ifstruct, and the LiquidAI/ifstruct-v1.0 dataset) is published openly and runnable end to end on free-tier hardware.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: Full reproducibility lowers due-diligence cost for anyone wanting to independently verify or extend the claimed gains before relying on them.
